title: Understanding MSE
text: To calculate the Mean Squared Error (MSE), you need to find the difference between the observed values and the predicted values from the regression line, square those differences, and then find the average of those squared differences.

title: Identifying Points
text: Look at the graph and identify the three data points. These points are where the observed values are plotted. You'll need these to calculate the differences from the predicted values.

title: Calculating Differences
text: What is the difference between the observed tip and the predicted tip for the first data point?

title: Squaring Differences
text: What is the square of the difference you calculated for the first data point?

title: Averaging Squared Differences
text: After calculating and squaring the differences for all data points, sum them up and divide by the number of data points to find the MSE.
